summary: Observation tower on Mont du Général-Allard at the Valcartier military base, Quebec; last tower in use in Quebec until 1981 per a 2015 blog.

facts.status_note: Described in the present tense in a 2015 blog post; no later source found.

staffing.status: in use until 1981, per blog; the watch after that is unclear

events.note: Blog says the tower was in use until 1981 and calls it the last tower in use in Quebec. The same post also says a watchman still had a reason to be there, so the end of the watch is unclear.

evidence.supports: Network began in 1910 with the first tower used to spot forest fires in Quebec, south of Lac Matapédia in Gaspésie
evidence.quote: La première tour utilisée pour la détection des feux de forêt en sol québécois a été inaugurée en 1910 au sud du lac Matapédia en Gaspésie.

evidence.supports: Network peaked in the late 1930s with more than 500 towers
evidence.quote: Le développement du réseau de tours atteint son apogée à la fin des années 1930 alors qu’il est constitué de plus de 500 tours.

evidence.supports: Towers were typically a steel frame with an octagonal wooden cab where the watchman worked
evidence.quote: Les tours sont généralement constituées d’une structure en acier où trône une cabine octogonale en bois.

evidence.supports: The cab is where the watchmen carry out their tasks
evidence.quote: C’est dans cet espace que les gardiens réalisent leurs tâches.

evidence.supports: Most towers were destroyed for safety reasons; a few still exist
evidence.quote: Il en existe encore quelques-unes à l’heure actuelle

evidence.supports: Most towers were destroyed for safety reasons
evidence.quote: bien que la majorité ait été détruite pour des raisons de sécurité.

evidence.supports: The post calls towers tours d'observation and says they were the pillar of Quebec's detection system
evidence.quote: Bien que les tours d’observation aient été le pilier du système québécois de détection des feux de forêt

evidence.supports: Tower is 60 feet (18.3 m) and sits on the summit of Mont Général Allard, described in the present tense
evidence.quote: Ses 60 pieds trônent au sommet du Mont Général Allard.

evidence.supports: Tower is on the Valcartier military base; in use until 1981; last tower in use in Quebec
evidence.quote: La dernière tour en utilisation au Québec est utilisée jusqu’en 1981 sur la base militaire de Valcartier.

evidence.supports: Detection aircraft are not allowed to patrol the area, so the watchman still has a reason to be there
evidence.quote: Les avions de détection n’étant pas autorisés à patrouiller dans cette zone, le gardien de tour y a encore sa raison d’être.

evidence.supports: Official name is Mont du Général-Allard, in the municipality of Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier
OpenStreetMap maps the spot as a fire lookout

corrections.why: The blog describes a tower 60 feet high with a cab on its summit ('Ses 60 pieds trônent au sommet du Mont Général Allard'). Human review needed: 'ground' may be a deliberate category for a non-tower lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The blog says the tower was in use until 1981 but later says the watchman still has a reason to be there. The story keeps 1981 as the last recorded use and flags the wording as unclear.

sources.title: Le métier de gardien de tour

notes_for_editor: Only the 2015 SOPFEU blog describes this tower. OpenStreetMap gives the position and the fire-lookout tag; the Commission de toponymie record confirms the official name and municipality. The 2015 date comes from the blog URL path (/2015/09/) and the post's own '25 septembre' date line; the year is not printed beside that date in the cached text. The brief's Department of National Defence affiliation was not verified; the blog only says 'base militaire de Valcartier'. Height: 60 ft converted to 18.3 m. The blog's wording (in use until 1981, but the watchman still has a reason to be there) is inconsistent; check CFB Valcartier or Quebec ministry records. Two WebSearch calls returned nothing on the tower's build date. Suggested next: BAnQ digitised newspapers (for example Le Soleil), the Répertoire du patrimoine culturel du Québec, and SOPFEU or the Société d'histoire forestière du Québec for a build year and photo. The blog's network history (first tower 1910, more than 500 towers by the late 1930s, aircraft replacing towers from the mid-1960s) is general and is not confirmed for this tower.
